items.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: We’ve known each other almost fifteen years... And we play together quite often both in a duo situation... I love playing with Ken.

ctx.x: Who are some of your favorite compatriots to work with these days?

Well let’s see, you just talked to one of them, Ken Peplowski. We’ve known each other almost fifteen years, probably about twelve or thirteen years. And we play together quite often both in a duo situation, which is a lot of fun, and next week we’re working a trio with Michael Moore and larger groups too, quartets and stuff like that. He’s great too © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

because we really do have like a musical conversation when we play. Either one of us can go any way at any time and the other person is fearless enough to attempt to follow or not, as the choice may be. And he’s got the flexibility on his instruments to pull off just about anything he thinks of. So I love playing with Ken. And Bucky I enjoy playing with. There’s a lot of different things. items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Howard and I love playing together. We’ve had a long musical relationship and we’ve done some duo records.

ctx.x: Well that’s great to hear, I’m glad you brought all that up. At these jazz parties, the audience we see at them seems to be, I see a lot of the same people, and I guess they’re pretty knowledgeable about the music. It seems to be somewhat of a social event, but they seem to be pretty knowledgeable about the music.

They are pretty knowledgeable, yeah. They tend to be a little bit conservative in their musical taste but if you accept the job you have to kind of play within those parameters. They’re not going to want to hear even Thelonious — you know like “Ugly Beauty” or something, or an Ornette Coleman tune. Although once in a while if I get in a set with Howard, Howard Alden or somebody like that, a sympathetic ear or a sympathetic musician, we will throw something at them like that, and cover it up with a bunch of tunes…

The first time we went to one I hadn’t even heard that these things existed and I was just, at first I was so impressed. I mean you could overhear people having conversations about this guy’s latest record and who was in the rhythm section and I’m looking at these people you know — this couple is 60 years old and they’re into this that much. And it’s great.
